design: Cross-sectional two-phase community-based study (poster abstract, Alzheimer's Association International Conference supplement)
outcome: Prevalence of dementia and its association with physical activity and age
prevalence_numbers: Overall dementia 6.0%; Alzheimer's disease 2.8%, vascular 1.3%, mixed 1.1%

design: Cross-sectional population-based household survey on association of physical activity with mental health (dementia, depression)
outcome: Dementia and depression scores (BOAS/Short-CARE GMS screening) in relation to physical activity (IPAQ)
prevalence_numbers: Dementia prevalence 13.8% (depression 19.7%) among 875 elderly

design: Cross-sectional population-based prevalence study (PIETA study, Caeté, Brazil), reported as a poster abstract (P3-163) in an Alzheimer's Association conference abstract book (2009 supplement).
outcome: Prevalence of dementia and of cognitive impairment no dementia (CIND).
prevalence_numbers: Dementia in 176 of 639 (27.5%); CIND in 166 (26.0%). Only 39 (6.1%) of dementia cases had a previous diagnosis.

design: Cross-sectional survey of cognitive impairment in an indigenous community (Mura ethnicity), Amazonas, Brazil
outcome: Cognitive impairment (MCI/CIND and dementia combined); dementia not separated from MCI.
prevalence_numbers: Cognitive impairment (not dementia): 43.3% (95%CI 36.6–49.7) in total sample aged 50+; 43.7% in those 60+; 51.1% in those 65+. No dementia-specific prevalence.

design: Prospective community cohort follow-up (incidence study) of the Tremembé Epidemiologic Study, with a baseline prevalence survey reported elsewhere
outcome: Incidence of dementia (per 1000 person-years); association of baseline CIND/SCD with incident dementia
prevalence_numbers: This report gives no original prevalence estimate. It only cites the baseline prevalence (17.5%, 95% CI 14.6–20.6, 110/630) from the earlier published prevalence study (ref 18). The new estimate is incidence: 26.1/1000 PY.

design: Cross-sectional community survey (cluster random sampling) in São Paulo, Brazil
outcome: Prevalence of cognitive and functional impairment (CFI), a broad construct that includes dementia, plus cognitive impairment alone and functional impairment alone.
prevalence_numbers: CFI prevalence 16% (95% CI 14.2-17.8) aged 60+; weighted 15.8% (13.8-17.8). Aged 65+: 18.1% (weighted 18%). Cognitive impairment 50.4%; functional impairment 19.6%. No dementia prevalence reported.

design: Cross-sectional observational study, first phase of an epidemiologic survey
outcome: Cognitive and functional impairment (MMSE below education-adjusted cut-off, PFAQ above 5), not dementia
prevalence_numbers: Cognitive and functional impairment 19.2% (141/735); 20.0% (126/630) in those aged 65 or older. These are not dementia prevalence.

design: Cross-sectional population-based household survey (SABE project, São Paulo, year 2000), descriptive health/living-conditions report
outcome: Cognitive impairment by modified MMSE (cutoff ≤12), MMSE+Pfeffer; depressive symptoms, chronic diseases, ADL/IADL, living arrangements, health service use, income
prevalence_numbers: Cognitive deterioration 6.9% by MMSE (4.2% at 60-74, 17.7% at 75+); 3.4% with MMSE + Pfeffer. These are cognitive impairment screening results, not dementia prevalence.

design: Cross-sectional community survey (cluster sampling) of cognitive and functional impairment (CFI) prevalence
outcome: Cognitive and functional impairment (CFI), a syndromic category not restricted to dementia (includes non-dementia conditions)
prevalence_numbers: CFI prevalence 18.9% (95% CI 16.63–21.16) aged 60+; 21.9% (95% CI 19.50–24.29) aged 65+. No dementia-specific prevalence.

design: Cross-sectional two-stage survey (baseline of FIBRA-RJ cohort): MMSE screening then clinical diagnostic evaluation with DSM-IV.
outcome: All-cause dementia syndrome (DSM-IV) and subtypes.
prevalence_numbers: Weighted prevalence 16.9% (95% CI 14.4–19.8); 115 cases among 683 evaluated; age-specific 4.4% (67–69) to 61.6% (>90).

design: Retrospective chart review of risk factors for vascular dementia in elderly psychiatric outpatients without dementia
outcome: Prevalence of risk factors for vascular dementia (hypertension, diabetes, etc.) and interventions; not dementia prevalence
prevalence_numbers: None for dementia; only risk-factor frequencies (e.g., hypertension 48.7%). Patients with dementia were excluded by design.

design: Population-based cross-sectional study (Pietà study, Caeté, Minas Gerais), reported only as Alzheimer's Association conference poster abstracts (P3-164, P3-165, plus the end of the dementia-prevalence abstract).
outcome: All-cause dementia, plus cognitive impairment no dementia (CIND). The related abstracts cover successful brain aging and psychiatric disorders.
prevalence_numbers: Dementia in 176 of 639 (27.5%). CIND in 166 (26.0%).

design: Cross-sectional community household survey in three districts of Rio de Janeiro (1989-1990), using the BOAS interview with CARE-derived organic brain syndrome (OBS) and depression scales.
outcome: Cognitive impairment, called organic brain syndrome (OBS), and depression. OBS was defined by a score above the 2/3 cutoff on the BOAS/CARE scale. This is not a dementia diagnosis.
prevalence_numbers: OBS (cognitive impairment) prevalence was 5.95% in Copacabana, 9.84% in Meier and 29.75% in Santa Cruz. These are screening-based cognitive impairment rates, not dementia prevalence.

design: Systematic review of prevalence studies (1990-2010), no pooled meta-analysis
outcome: Dementia prevalence as reported in the included primary studies
prevalence_numbers: Five high-quality São Paulo studies reported 5.1% to 19.0%. No overall pooled estimate was produced.

design: Cross-sectional baseline analysis of an ongoing multicentre prospective cohort (CHANGE Study), reported as a poster/conference abstract
outcome: Prevalence of diagnosed and undiagnosed dementia at hospital admission, and associated adverse outcomes (length of stay, delirium, mortality)
prevalence_numbers: Diagnosed dementia 230 (27%); undiagnosed dementia 122 (14%); 35% of patients with preexisting dementia were undiagnosed (hospital sample)

design: Two-phase cross-sectional community-based study (poster/conference abstract, Alzheimer's & Dementia 2023 Suppl.)
outcome: Dementia prevalence and its association with physical activity and age; subtypes (AD, vascular, mixed)
prevalence_numbers: Overall dementia 6.0%; AD 2.8%; vascular 1.3%; mixed 1.1%

design: Cross-sectional analysis of baseline data from ELSI-Brazil (poster/conference abstract), examining association of age of literacy with CIND and dementia prevalence ratios
outcome: Prevalence ratios of CIND and dementia by literacy age group (risk-factor analysis)
prevalence_numbers: 6% with dementia and 8% with CIND in the sample of 5,244 (unweighted descriptive, mentioned in the abstract)

design: Conference abstract (podium presentation) of a cohort study using ELSA data (English Longitudinal Study of Ageing); 17-year follow-up.
outcome: Association of physical activity with incident all-cause dementia (odds), over 17 years.
prevalence_numbers: Only cumulative 17-year diagnosis of 7.8% (95% CI 7.3 to 8.4) in an English cohort; not a point prevalence in Brazilians.

design: Single-center descriptive analysis of health records; conference poster abstract
outcome: Clinical characteristics and dementia subtype distribution of referred patients
prevalence_numbers: None for the general population. The abstract cites a 17.5% prevalence from the Tremembe study, but that is background, not original data.

design: Cross-sectional descriptive study (conference poster abstract)
outcome: Altered MMSE cognitive screening and its association with 12 modifiable dementia risk factors (e.g. education)
prevalence_numbers: No dementia prevalence reported. Only proportions with altered MMSE by education level (47.6% of illiterate; 82.8% of those with 1-4 years schooling).

design: Cross-sectional community survey (Aug 2021–Jan 2022) of dementia and CIND in an urban Indigenous community in Manaus, Brazil.
outcome: Dementia and cognitive impairment no dementia (CIND), plus associated factors.

design: Prospective clinical case series of demented outpatients with follow-up for reversibility
outcome: Potentially reversible causes of dementia and their treatment outcome at follow-up
prevalence_numbers: No population prevalence of dementia. Only the proportion with potentially reversible causes among clinic dementia patients (26 of 110) and a 10% figure cited from the literature.

design: Retrospective and prospective case-series of dementia patients at a tertiary university hospital (HC-UNICAMP), 1989-1998, describing etiological subtypes
outcome: Relative frequency of dementia subtypes (vascular, Alzheimer, etc.) among hospital dementia patients
prevalence_numbers: No population prevalence; only subtype proportions among 261 hospital cases (vascular 24.9%, Alzheimer 23.7%).

design: Prospective clinical case series of demented outpatients with follow-up for reversibility
outcome: Potentially reversible causes of dementia and treatment outcome at follow-up
prevalence_numbers: No population prevalence of dementia reported; only proportions of reversible causes among demented patients (26/110).

design: Retrospective single-center descriptive analysis of medical records from a dementia outpatient clinic
outcome: Clinical and demographic characteristics, comorbidities, dementia stage, etiologic diagnoses and neuroimaging of clinic patients
prevalence_numbers: No population prevalence; only proportions of diagnoses among clinic patients (e.g., AD 31%, FTD 14%)

design: Retrospective chart review of risk factors for vascular dementia
outcome: Prevalence of risk factors for vascular dementia (hypertension, diabetes, etc.) and interventions; not dementia
prevalence_numbers: None for dementia. Risk factor prevalences only (e.g., hypertension 48.7%, at least one risk factor 86%).

design: Cross-sectional two-stage study (screening then diagnostic assessment) of hospital inpatients
outcome: Dementia (DSM-IV) and cognitive and functional impairment (CFI) among inpatients; association with clinical and sociodemographic variables
prevalence_numbers: Dementia 17.2% (95% CI 12.3-22.1; 31 cases); CFI 37.4% (95% CI 31.1-43.7) among inpatients

design: Cross-sectional analysis of ELSI-Brazil baseline (2015-2016) examining socioeconomic determinants (multinomial regression) of CIND and dementia
outcome: Odds of CIND and dementia (vs normal cognition) in relation to life-course socioeconomic factors (education, food insecurity, employment stability, income)
prevalence_numbers: No prevalence estimate reported. Table 1 gives unweighted counts: dementia N=364 of 5,249 (about 6.9% crude unweighted, not a reported estimate); weighted prevalence is in the separate Bertola 2023 paper.

design: Cross-sectional, one-phase population survey (São Paulo Ageing & Health Study, SPAH); secondary analysis of anemia–dementia association
outcome: Association between anemia (WHO) and all-cause dementia (DSM-IV, 10/66 protocol) and subtypes
prevalence_numbers: Dementia in 99/1948 (5.1%) of the analysed subsample (those with a valid blood count). It is not the full-sample SPAH estimate and is not age-standardised.

design: Cross-sectional population-based diagnostic accuracy (MMSE validation) study using SPAH baseline data
outcome: Psychometric properties (sensitivity, specificity, ROC) of the MMSE against DSM-IV dementia; determinants of MMSE scores
prevalence_numbers: 84/1,933 (4.4%) DSM-IV dementia in the analysed subsample (6.3% no education, 3.1% with education). This is not a full-sample estimate: 139 were excluded, including 18 dementia cases. The SPAH prevalence is reported in a separate paper (ref 34).

design: Retrospective/prospective case series of dementia patients at a tertiary university hospital (UNICAMP), 1989-1998, describing etiological subtypes.
outcome: Relative frequency of dementia subtypes (vascular, Alzheimer, hydrocephalic, etc.) among hospital dementia patients.
prevalence_numbers: No population prevalence; only subtype proportions among 261 hospital patients (vascular 24.9%, Alzheimer 23.7%).

design: Retrospective chart review of outpatients at a dementia clinic (1991-2001)
outcome: Proportion of potentially reversible dementias among clinic dementia patients; etiologic distribution of dementia
prevalence_numbers: 8.0% of dementia cases (22/275) were potentially reversible; 4.8% of all patients seen. No community prevalence of dementia.
